units.leftText: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
units.rightText: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

units.leftText: The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with some of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god. He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
units.rightText: And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, along with some of the articles from the house of God. He carried these off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, where he put them in the treasury of his god.
rightNotes: 1:2 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: The king spoke to Ashpenaz, the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring in some of the children of Israel, even of the royal offspring and of the nobles:
units.rightText: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—
rightNotes: 1:3 Hebrew from the seed of the kingdom

units.leftText: youths in whom was no defect, but well-favored, skillful in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge, understanding science, and who had the ability to stand in the king’s palace; and that he should teach them the learning and the language of the Chaldeans.
units.rightText: young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace— and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
rightNotes: 1:4 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s delicacies and of the wine which he drank, and that they should be nourished three years, that at its end they should stand before the king.
units.rightText: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.

units.leftText: Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
units.rightText: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

units.leftText: The prince of the eunuchs gave names to them: to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
units.rightText: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

units.leftText: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
units.rightText: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.

units.leftText: Now God made Daniel find kindness and compassion in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs.
units.rightText: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,

units.leftText: The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and your drink. For why should he see your faces worse looking than the youths who are of your own age? Then you would endanger my head with the king.”
units.rightText: but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”

units.leftText: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
units.rightText: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

units.leftText: “Test your servants, I beg you, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
units.rightText: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.

units.leftText: Then let our faces be examined before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s delicacies; and as you see, deal with your servants.”
units.rightText: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”

units.leftText: So he listened to them in this matter, and tested them for ten days.
units.rightText: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.

units.leftText: At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer and they were fatter in flesh than all the youths who ate of the king’s delicacies.
units.rightText: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.

units.leftText: So the steward took away their delicacies and the wine that they were given to drink, and gave them vegetables.
units.rightText: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.

units.leftText: Now as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
units.rightText: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.

units.leftText: At the end of the days which the king had appointed for bringing them in, the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
units.rightText: Now at the end of the time specified by the king, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.

units.leftText: The king talked with them; and among them all was found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Therefore they stood before the king.
units.rightText: And the king spoke with them, and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.

units.leftText: In every matter of wisdom and understanding concerning which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his realm.
units.rightText: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.

units.leftText: Daniel continued even to the first year of King Cyrus.
units.rightText: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.

units.leftText: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him.
units.rightText: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled his spirit, and sleep escaped him.

units.leftText: Then the king commanded that the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
units.rightText: So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain his dreams. When they came and stood before the king,

units.leftText: The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.”
units.rightText: he said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”

units.leftText: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”
units.rightText: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, “O king, may you live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation.”

units.leftText: The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill.
units.rightText: The king replied to the astrologers, “My word is final: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut into pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.

units.leftText: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, rewards, and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.”
units.rightText: But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”

units.leftText: They answered the second time and said, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”
units.rightText: They answered a second time, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will give the interpretation.”

units.leftText: The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.
units.rightText: The king replied, “I know for sure that you are stalling for time because you see that my word is final.

units.leftText: But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the situation changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can show me its interpretation.”
units.rightText: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one decree for you. You have conspired to speak before me false and fraudulent words, hoping the situation will change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation.”

units.leftText: The Chaldeans answered the king and said, “There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler has asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
units.rightText: The astrologers answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king requests! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.

units.leftText: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”
units.rightText: What the king requests is so difficult that no one can tell it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”

units.leftText: Because of this, the king was angry and very furious, and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
units.rightText: This response made the king so angry and furious that he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.

units.leftText: So the decree went out, and the wise men were to be slain. They sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
units.rightText: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be executed, and men went to look for Daniel and his friends to execute them.

units.leftText: Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
units.rightText: When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, went out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel responded with discretion and tact.

units.leftText: He answered Arioch the king’s captain, “Why is the decree so urgent from the king?” Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
units.rightText: “Why is the decree from the king so harsh?” he asked.

units.leftText: Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
units.rightText: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him some time, so that he could give him the interpretation.

units.leftText: Then Daniel went to his house and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:
units.rightText: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

units.leftText: that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret, that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
units.rightText: urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

units.leftText: Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
units.rightText: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven

units.leftText: Daniel answered,
units.rightText: and declared:

units.leftText: He changes the times and the seasons.
units.rightText: He changes the times and seasons;

units.leftText: He reveals the deep and secret things.
units.rightText: He reveals the deep and hidden things;

units.leftText: I thank you and praise you,
units.rightText: To You, O God of my fathers,

units.leftText: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.”
units.rightText: Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon! Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation.”

units.leftText: Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and said this to him: “I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judah who will make known to the king the interpretation.”
units.rightText: Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”

units.leftText: The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?”
units.rightText: The king responded to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to tell me what I saw in the dream, as well as its interpretation?”

units.leftText: Daniel answered before the king, and said, “The secret which the king has demanded can’t be shown to the king by wise men, enchanters, magicians, or soothsayers;
units.rightText: Daniel answered the king, “No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires.

units.leftText: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed are these:
units.rightText: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed were these:

units.leftText: “As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen.
units.rightText: As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to the future, and the Revealer of Mysteries made known to you what will happen.

units.leftText: But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
units.rightText: And to me this mystery has been revealed, not because I have more wisdom than any man alive, but in order that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.

units.leftText: “You, O king, saw, and behold, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying.
units.rightText: As you, O king, were watching, a great statue appeared. A great and dazzling statue stood before you, and its form was awesome.
leftNotes: 2:31 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
rightNotes: 2:31 Or image; here and through the rest of Daniel 2

units.leftText: As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
units.rightText: The head of the statue was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze,

units.leftText: its legs of iron, its feet part of iron and part of clay.
units.rightText: its legs were iron, and its feet were part iron and part clay.

units.leftText: You saw until a stone was cut out without hands, which struck the image on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.
units.rightText: As you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them.
rightNotes: 2:34 LXX cut out from a mountain

units.leftText: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
units.rightText: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered and became like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

units.leftText: “This is the dream; and we will tell its interpretation before the king.
units.rightText: This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.

units.leftText: You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.
units.rightText: You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given sovereignty, power, strength, and glory.

units.leftText: Wherever the children of men dwell, he has given the animals of the field and the birds of the sky into your hand, and has made you rule over them all. You are the head of gold.
units.rightText: Wherever the sons of men or beasts of the field or birds of the air dwell, He has given them into your hand and has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.

units.leftText: “After you, another kingdom will arise that is inferior to you; and another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
units.rightText: But after you, there will arise another kingdom, inferior to yours.

units.leftText: The fourth kingdom will be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, it will break in pieces and crush.
units.rightText: Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom as strong as iron; for iron shatters and crushes all things, and like iron that crushes all things, it will shatter and crush all the others.

units.leftText: Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay and part of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but there will be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.
units.rightText: And just as you saw that the feet and toes were made partly of fired clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom, yet some of the strength of iron will be in it — just as you saw the iron mixed with clay.

units.leftText: As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
units.rightText: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.

units.leftText: Whereas you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they will mingle themselves with the seed of men; but they won’t cling to one another, even as iron does not mix with clay.
units.rightText: As you saw the iron mixed with clay, so the peoples will mix with one another but will not hold together any more than iron mixes with clay.
rightNotes: 2:43 Aramaic the seed of men

units.leftText: “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, nor will its sovereignty be left to another people; but it will break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.
units.rightText: In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.

units.leftText: Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.”
units.rightText: And just as you saw a stone being cut out of the mountain without human hands, and it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold, so the great God has told the king what will happen in the future.

units.leftText: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, worshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odors to him.
units.rightText: At this, King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, paid homage to Daniel, and ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.

units.leftText: The king answered to Daniel, and said, “Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.”
units.rightText: The king said to Daniel, “Your God is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings, the Revealer of Mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”

units.leftText: Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.
units.rightText: Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many generous gifts. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief administrator over all the wise men of Babylon.

units.leftText: Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon, but Daniel was in the king’s gate.
units.rightText: And at Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained in the king’s court.

units.leftText: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was sixty cubits and its width six cubits. He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
units.rightText: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

units.rightText: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other officials of the provinces to attend the dedication of the statue he had set up.

units.rightText: So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the rulers of the provinces assembled for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.

units.rightText: Therefore, as soon as all the people heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and all kinds of music, the people of every nation and language would fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

units.rightText: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.

units.rightText: At this, Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and the expression on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual,

units.leftText: These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
units.rightText: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, firmly bound, fell into the blazing fiery furnace.

units.leftText: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?”
units.rightText: Suddenly King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up in amazement and asked his advisers, “Did we not throw three men, firmly bound, into the fire?”

units.leftText: He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods. ”
units.rightText: “Look!” he exclaimed. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire — and the fourth looks like a son of the gods! ”
rightNotes: 3:25 Or like the Son of God

units.leftText: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace. He spoke and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here!”
units.rightText: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the blazing fiery furnace and called out, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!”

units.leftText: The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed. The smell of fire wasn’t even on them.
units.rightText: and when the satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers had gathered around, they saw that the fire had no effect on the bodies of these men. Not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of fire on them.

units.leftText: Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and have yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god except their own God.
units.rightText: Nebuchadnezzar declared, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him. They violated the king’s command and risked their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.
rightNotes: 3:28 Or Angel

units.leftText: Therefore I make a decree that every people, nation, and language which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill, because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”
units.rightText: Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. For there is no other god who can deliver in this way.”

units.leftText: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
units.rightText: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

units.leftText: Nebuchadnezzar the king,
units.rightText: King Nebuchadnezzar,

units.leftText: It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Most High God has worked toward me.
units.rightText: I am pleased to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me.

units.leftText: How great are his signs!
units.rightText: How great are His signs,

units.leftText: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
units.rightText: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.

units.leftText: I saw a dream which made me afraid; and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
units.rightText: I had a dream, and it frightened me; while I was in my bed, the images and visions in my mind alarmed me.

units.leftText: Therefore I made a decree to bring in all the wise men of Babylon before me, that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
units.rightText: So I issued a decree that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to interpret the dream for me.

units.leftText: Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers came in; and I told them the dream, but they didn’t make known to me its interpretation.
units.rightText: When the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and diviners came in, I told them the dream, but they could not interpret it for me.
rightNotes: 4:7 Or Chaldeans

units.leftText: But at last, Daniel came in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. I told the dream before him, saying,
units.rightText: But at last, into my presence came Daniel (whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods). And I told him the dream:

units.leftText: “Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.
units.rightText: “O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery baffles you. So explain to me the visions I saw in my dream, and their interpretation.

units.leftText: These were the visions of my head on my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the middle of the earth; and its height was great.
units.rightText: In these visions of my mind as I was lying in bed, I saw this come to pass:

units.leftText: The tree grew and was strong. Its height reached to the sky and its sight to the end of all the earth.
units.rightText: The tree grew large and strong;

units.leftText: Its leaves were beautiful, and it had much fruit, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field had shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
units.rightText: Its leaves were beautiful,

units.leftText: “I saw in the visions of my head on my bed, and behold, a holy watcher came down from the sky.
units.rightText: As I lay on my bed, I also saw in the visions of my mind a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
rightNotes: 4:13 Or an angelic watcher or a messenger; also in verses 17 and 23

units.leftText: He cried aloud and said this: ‘Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches! Shake off its leaves and scatter its fruit! Let the animals get away from under it and the birds from its branches.
units.rightText: He called out in a loud voice:

units.leftText: Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky. Let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.
units.rightText: But leave the stump with its roots in the ground,

units.leftText: Let his heart be changed from man’s, and let an animal’s heart be given to him. Then let seven times pass over him.
units.rightText: Let his mind be changed from that of a man,

units.leftText: “‘The sentence is by the decree of the watchers and the demand by the word of the holy ones, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will, and sets up over it the lowest of men.’
units.rightText: This decision is the decree of the watchers,

units.leftText: “This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
units.rightText: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me the interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can interpret it for me. But you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”

units.leftText: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The king answered, “Belteshazzar, don’t let the dream or the interpretation trouble you.”
units.rightText: For a time, Daniel, who was also known as Belteshazzar, was perplexed, and his thoughts alarmed him.

units.leftText: The tree that you saw, which grew and was strong, whose height reached to the sky and its sight to all the earth;
units.rightText: The tree you saw that grew large and strong, whose top reached the sky and was visible to all the earth,

units.leftText: whose leaves were beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and in it was food for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had their habitation—
units.rightText: whose foliage was beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, providing food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived, and in whose branches the birds of the air nested—

units.leftText: it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
units.rightText: you, O king, are that tree! For you have become great and strong; your greatness has grown to reach the sky, and your dominion extends to the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: “Whereas the king saw a holy watcher coming down from the sky and saying, ‘Cut down the tree, and destroy it; nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky. Let his portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over him.’
units.rightText: And you, O king, saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying:

units.leftText: “This is the interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High, which has come on my lord the king:
units.rightText: This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree that the Most High has issued against my lord the king:

units.leftText: You will be driven from men and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass as oxen, and will be wet with the dew of the sky, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.
units.rightText: You will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will feed on grass like an ox and be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.

units.leftText: Whereas it was commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree, your kingdom will be restored to you after you learn that Heaven rules.
units.rightText: As for the command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots, your kingdom will be restored to you as soon as you acknowledge that Heaven rules.

units.leftText: Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.”
units.rightText: Therefore, may my advice be pleasing to you, O king. Break away from your sins by doing what is right, and from your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed. Perhaps there will be an extension of your prosperity.”

units.leftText: All this came on the King Nebuchadnezzar.
units.rightText: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.

units.leftText: At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
units.rightText: Twelve months later, as he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,

units.leftText: The king spoke and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
units.rightText: the king exclaimed, “Is this not Babylon the Great, which I myself have built as a royal residence by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”

units.leftText: While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.
units.rightText: While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven: “It is decreed to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, that the kingdom has departed from you.

units.leftText: You shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field. You shall be made to eat grass like oxen. Seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.’”
units.rightText: You will be driven away from mankind to live with the beasts of the field, and you will feed on grass like an ox. And seven times will pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.”

units.leftText: This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men and ate grass like oxen; and his body was wet with the dew of the sky until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.
units.rightText: At that moment the sentence against Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from mankind. He ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.

units.leftText: At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever,
units.rightText: But at the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was restored to me. Then I praised the Most High, and I honored and glorified Him who lives forever:

units.leftText: All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing;
units.rightText: All the peoples of the earth

units.leftText: At the same time my understanding returned to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and brightness returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent greatness was added to me.
units.rightText: At the same time my sanity was restored, my honor and splendor returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my throne, and surpassing greatness was added to me.

units.leftText: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.
units.rightText: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.

units.leftText: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.
units.rightText: Later, King Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine with them.
rightNotes: 5:1 Aramaic does not include Later. Some translators include Many years later to account for the time elapsed, probably about 30 years, since the previous chapter.

units.leftText: Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine, commanded that the golden and silver vessels which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem be brought to him, that the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, might drink from them.
units.rightText: Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring in the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king could drink from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
rightNotes: 5:2 Or predecessor or grandfather; also in verses 11, 13, and 18

units.leftText: Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of God’s house which was at Jerusalem; and the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, drank from them.
units.rightText: Thus they brought in the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king drank from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.

units.leftText: They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
units.rightText: As they drank the wine, they praised their gods of gold and silver, bronze and iron, wood and stone.

units.leftText: In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
units.rightText: At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. As the king watched the hand that was writing,

units.leftText: Then the king’s face was changed in him, and his thoughts troubled him; and the joints of his thighs were loosened, and his knees struck one against another.
units.rightText: his face grew pale and his thoughts so alarmed him that his hips gave way and his knees knocked together.

units.leftText: The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. The king spoke and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and shows me its interpretation shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”
units.rightText: The king called out for the enchanters, astrologers, and diviners to be brought in, and he said to these wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this inscription and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around his neck, and he will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
rightNotes: 5:7 Or Chaldeans; also in verse 11

units.leftText: Then all the king’s wise men came in; but they could not read the writing, and couldn’t make known to the king the interpretation.
units.rightText: So all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the inscription or interpret it for him.

units.leftText: Then King Belshazzar was greatly troubled, and his face was changed in him, and his lords were perplexed.
units.rightText: Then King Belshazzar became even more terrified, his face grew even more pale, and his nobles were bewildered.

units.leftText: The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house. The queen spoke and said, “O king, live forever; don’t let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed.
units.rightText: Hearing the outcry of the king and his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. “O king, may you live forever!” she said. “Do not let your thoughts terrify you, or your face grow pale.
rightNotes: 5:10 Or queen mother

units.leftText: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father, light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. The king, Nebuchadnezzar, your father—yes, the king, your father—made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers,
units.rightText: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the days of your father he was found to have insight, intelligence, and wisdom like that of the gods.

units.leftText: because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.”
units.rightText: did this because Daniel, the one he named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, as well as knowledge, understanding, and the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve difficult problems. Summon Daniel, therefore, and he will give you the interpretation.”

units.leftText: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Are you that Daniel of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Judah?
units.rightText: So Daniel was brought before the king, who asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?

units.leftText: I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you and that light, understanding, and excellent wisdom are found in you.
units.rightText: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that you have insight, intelligence, and extraordinary wisdom.

units.leftText: Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing, and make known to me its interpretation; but they could not show the interpretation of the thing.
units.rightText: Now the wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this inscription and interpret it for me, but they could not give its interpretation.

units.leftText: But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations and dissolve doubts. Now if you can read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold around your neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”
units.rightText: But I have heard about you, that you are able to give interpretations and solve difficult problems. Therefore, if you can read this inscription and give me its interpretation, you will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”

units.leftText: Then Daniel answered before the king, “Let your gifts be to yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
units.rightText: In response, Daniel said to the king, “You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Nevertheless, I will read the inscription for the king and interpret it for him.

units.leftText: “To you, king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty.
units.rightText: As for you, O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness, glory and honor.

units.leftText: Because of the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. He killed whom he wanted to, and he kept alive whom he wanted to. He raised up whom he wanted to, and he put down whom he wanted to.
units.rightText: Because of the greatness that He bestowed on him, the people of every nation and language trembled in fear before him. He killed whom he wished and kept alive whom he wished; he exalted whom he wished and humbled whom he wished.

units.leftText: But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him.
units.rightText: But when his heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.

units.leftText: He was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will.
units.rightText: He was driven away from mankind, and his mind was like that of a beast. He lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind, setting over it whom He wishes.

units.leftText: “You, his son, Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this,
units.rightText: But you his son, O Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.
rightNotes: 5:22 Or descendant or successor or grandson

units.leftText: but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which don’t see, or hear, or know; and you have not glorified the God in whose hand your breath is, and whose are all your ways.
units.rightText: Instead, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels from His house were brought to you, and as you drank wine from them with your nobles, wives, and concubines, you praised your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you have failed to glorify the God who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways.

units.leftText: Then the part of the hand was sent from before him, and this writing was inscribed.
units.rightText: Therefore He sent the hand that wrote the inscription.

units.leftText: “This is the writing that was inscribed: ‘MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.’
units.rightText: Now this is the inscription that was written:

units.leftText: “This is the interpretation of the thing:
units.rightText: And this is the interpretation of the message:

units.leftText: TEKEL: you are weighed in the balances, and are found wanting.
units.rightText: TEKEL means that you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.
rightNotes: 5:27 Tekel sounds like the Aramaic for weighed.

units.leftText: PERES: your kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.”
units.rightText: PERES means that your kingdom has been divided and given over to the Medes and Persians.”
rightNotes: 5:28 Peres (the singular of Parsin) sounds like the Aramaic for divided and for Persia.

units.leftText: Then Belshazzar commanded, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.
units.rightText: Then Belshazzar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel in purple, placed a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed him the third highest ruler in the kingdom.

units.leftText: In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean King was slain.
units.rightText: That very night Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans was slain,
rightNotes: 5:30 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.
units.rightText: and Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.

units.leftText: It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom one hundred twenty local governors, who should be throughout the whole kingdom;
units.rightText: Now it pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,

units.leftText: and over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one, that these local governors might give account to them, and that the king should suffer no loss.
units.rightText: and over them three administrators, including Daniel, to whom these satraps were accountable so that the king would not suffer loss.

units.leftText: Then this Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and the local governors, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
units.rightText: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

units.leftText: Then the presidents and the local governors sought to find occasion against Daniel as touching the kingdom; but they could find no occasion or fault, because he was faithful. There wasn’t any error or fault found in him.
units.rightText: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.

units.leftText: Then these men said, “We won’t find any occasion against this Daniel, unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.”
units.rightText: Finally these men said, “We will never find any charge against this Daniel unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”

units.leftText: Then these presidents and local governors assembled together to the king, and said this to him, “King Darius, live forever!
units.rightText: So the administrators and satraps went together to the king and said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!

units.leftText: All the presidents of the kingdom, the deputies and the local governors, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to make a strong decree, that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
units.rightText: All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish an ordinance and enforce a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.

units.leftText: Now, O king, establish the decree and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”
units.rightText: Therefore, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so that it cannot be changed — in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”

units.leftText: Therefore King Darius signed the writing and the decree.
units.rightText: Therefore King Darius signed the written decree.

units.leftText: When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.
units.rightText: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.

units.leftText: Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.
units.rightText: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel petitioning and imploring his God.

units.leftText: Then they came near, and spoke before the king concerning the king’s decree: “Haven’t you signed a decree that every man who makes a petition to any god or man within thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?”
units.rightText: So they approached the king and asked about his royal decree: “Did you not sign a decree that for thirty days any man who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions?”

units.leftText: Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
units.rightText: Then they told the king, “Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, shows no regard for you, O king, or for the decree that you have signed. He still makes his petition three times a day.”

units.leftText: Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.
units.rightText: As soon as the king heard this, he was deeply distressed and set his mind on delivering Daniel, and he labored until sundown to rescue him.

units.leftText: Then these men assembled together to the king, and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.”
units.rightText: Then the men approached the king together and said to him, “Remember, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no decree or ordinance established by the king can be changed.”

units.leftText: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.”
units.rightText: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions.

units.leftText: A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
units.rightText: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.

units.leftText: Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting. No musical instruments were brought before him; and his sleep fled from him.
units.rightText: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.

units.leftText: Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste to the den of lions.
units.rightText: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.

units.leftText: When he came near to Daniel in the den, he cried with a troubled voice. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, is your God, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the lions?”
units.rightText: When he reached the den, he cried out in a voice of anguish, “O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?”

units.leftText: Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!
units.rightText: Then Daniel replied, “O king, may you live forever!

units.leftText: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me, because innocence was found in me before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”
units.rightText: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, for I was found innocent in His sight, and I have done no wrong against you, O king.”

units.leftText: Then the king was exceedingly glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
units.rightText: The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den, and when Daniel was lifted out of the den, no wounds whatsoever were found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

units.leftText: The king commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions—them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke all their bones in pieces before they came to the bottom of the den.
units.rightText: At the command of the king, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions— they and their children and wives. And before they had reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

units.leftText: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth:
units.rightText: Then King Darius wrote to the people of every nation and language throughout the land: “May your prosperity abound.

units.leftText: “I make a decree that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel.
units.rightText: I hereby decree that in every part of my kingdom, men are to tremble in fear before the God of Daniel:

units.leftText: He delivers and rescues.
units.rightText: He delivers and rescues;

units.leftText: So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
units.rightText: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
rightNotes: 6:28 Or prospered during the reign of Darius, that is, the reign of Cyrus

units.leftText: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions of his head while on his bed. Then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters.
units.rightText: In the first year of the reign of Belshazzar over Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and visions passed through his mind as he lay on his bed. He wrote down the dream, and this is the summary of his account.

units.leftText: Daniel spoke and said, “I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea.
units.rightText: Daniel declared: “In my vision in the night I looked, and suddenly the four winds of heaven were churning up the great sea.
rightNotes: 7:2 Perhaps the Great Sea, that is, the Mediterranean Sea

units.leftText: Four great animals came up from the sea, different from one another.
units.rightText: Then four great beasts came up out of the sea, each one different from the others:

units.leftText: “The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings. I watched until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth and made to stand on two feet as a man. A man’s heart was given to it.
units.rightText: The first beast was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man and given the mind of a man.

units.leftText: “Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’
units.rightText: Suddenly another beast appeared, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. So it was told, ‘Get up and gorge yourself on flesh!’

units.leftText: “After this I saw, and behold, another, like a leopard, which had on its back four wings of a bird. The animal also had four heads; and dominion was given to it.
units.rightText: Next, as I watched, suddenly another beast appeared. It was like a leopard, and on its back it had four wings like those of a bird. The beast also had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.

units.leftText: “After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there was a fourth animal, awesome, powerful, and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet. It was different from all the animals that were before it. It had ten horns.
units.rightText: After this, as I watched in my vision in the night, suddenly a fourth beast appeared, and it was terrifying — dreadful and extremely strong — with large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed; then it trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

units.leftText: “I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots; and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking arrogantly.
units.rightText: While I was contemplating the horns, suddenly another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like those of a man and a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.

units.leftText: “I watched until thrones were placed,
units.rightText: As I continued to watch,

units.leftText: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him.
units.rightText: A river of fire was flowing,

units.leftText: “I watched at that time because of the voice of the arrogant words which the horn spoke. I watched even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
units.rightText: Then I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. As I continued to watch, the beast was slain, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the animals, their dominion was taken away; yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
units.rightText: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed, but they were granted an extension of life for a season and a time.

units.leftText: “I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him.
units.rightText: In my vision in the night I continued to watch,

units.leftText: Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed.
units.rightText: And He was given dominion,

units.leftText: “As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved within my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.
units.rightText: I, Daniel, was grieved in my spirit, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.

units.leftText: I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this.
units.rightText: I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.

units.leftText: ‘These great animals, which are four, are four kings, who will arise out of the earth.
units.rightText: ‘These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.

units.leftText: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’
units.rightText: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever — yes, forever and ever.’

units.leftText: “Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was different from all of them, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of bronze; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;
units.rightText: Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others — extremely terrifying — devouring and crushing with iron teeth and bronze claws, then trampling underfoot whatever was left.

units.leftText: and concerning the ten horns that were on its head and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes and a mouth that spoke arrogantly, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
units.rightText: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell— the horn whose appearance was more imposing than the others, with eyes and with a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.

units.leftText: I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them,
units.rightText: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them,

units.leftText: until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.
units.rightText: until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for them to possess the kingdom.

units.leftText: “So he said, ‘The fourth animal will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms, and will devour the whole earth, and will tread it down and break it in pieces.
units.rightText: This is what he said: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on the earth, different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.

units.leftText: As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings.
units.rightText: And the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king, different from the earlier ones, will rise and subdue three kings.

units.leftText: He will speak words against the Most High, and will wear out the saints of the Most High. He will plan to change the times and the law; and they will be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
units.rightText: He will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High, intending to change the appointed times and laws; and the saints will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.

units.leftText: “‘But the judgment will be set, and they will take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it to the end.
units.rightText: But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.

units.leftText: The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.’
units.rightText: Then the sovereignty, dominion, and greatness of the kingdoms under all of heaven will be given to the people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey Him.’

units.leftText: “Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face was changed in me; but I kept the matter in my heart.”
units.rightText: Thus ends the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale. But I kept the matter to myself.”

units.leftText: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, even to me, Daniel, after that which appeared to me at the first.
units.rightText: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.

units.leftText: I saw the vision. Now it was so, that when I saw, I was in the citadel of Susa, which is in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision, and I was by the river Ulai.
units.rightText: And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.

units.leftText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a ram which had two horns stood before the river. The two horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last.
units.rightText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.

units.leftText: I saw the ram pushing westward, northward, and southward. No animals could stand before him. There wasn’t any who could deliver out of his hand, but he did according to his will, and magnified himself.
units.rightText: I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.

units.leftText: As I was considering, behold, a male goat came from the west over the surface of the whole earth, and didn’t touch the ground. The goat had a notable horn between his eyes.
units.rightText: As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.

units.leftText: He came to the ram that had the two horns, which I saw standing before the river, and ran on him in the fury of his power.
units.rightText: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.

units.leftText: I saw him come close to the ram, and he was moved with anger against him, and struck the ram, and broke his two horns. There was no power in the ram to stand before him; but he cast him down to the ground and trampled on him. There was no one who could deliver the ram out of his hand.
units.rightText: I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.

units.leftText: The male goat magnified himself exceedingly. When he was strong, the great horn was broken; and instead of it there came up four notable horns toward the four winds of the sky.
units.rightText: Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.

units.leftText: Out of one of them came out a little horn which grew exceedingly great—toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the glorious land.
units.rightText: From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.

units.leftText: It grew great, even to the army of the sky; and it cast down some of the army and of the stars to the ground and trampled on them.
units.rightText: It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth and trampled them.

units.leftText: Yes, it magnified itself, even to the prince of the army; and it took away from him the continual burnt offering, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.
units.rightText: It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.

units.leftText: The army was given over to it together with the continual burnt offering through disobedience. It cast down truth to the ground, and it did its pleasure and prospered.
units.rightText: And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.
rightNotes: 8:12 Or on account of transgression

units.leftText: Then I heard a holy one speaking; and another holy one said to that certain one who spoke, “How long will the vision about the continual burnt offering, and the disobedience that makes desolate, to give both the sanctuary and the army to be trodden under foot be?”
units.rightText: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”

units.leftText: He said to me, “To two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary will be cleansed.”
units.rightText: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.”

units.leftText: When I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought to understand it. Then behold, there stood before me someone with the appearance of a man.
units.rightText: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.

units.leftText: I heard a man’s voice between the banks of the Ulai, which called and said, “Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.”
units.rightText: And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”

units.leftText: So he came near where I stood; and when he came, I was frightened, and fell on my face; but he said to me, “Understand, son of man, for the vision belongs to the time of the end.”
units.rightText: As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown.

units.leftText: Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face toward the ground; but he touched me and set me upright.
units.rightText: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.

units.leftText: He said, “Behold, I will make you know what will be in the latter time of the indignation, for it belongs to the appointed time of the end.
units.rightText: and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.

units.leftText: The ram which you saw, that had the two horns, they are the kings of Media and Persia.
units.rightText: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.

units.leftText: The rough male goat is the king of Greece. The great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.
units.rightText: The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
rightNotes: 8:21 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: As for that which was broken, in the place where four stood up, four kingdoms will stand up out of the nation, but not with his power.
units.rightText: The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation but will not have the same power.

units.leftText: “In the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors have come to the full, a king of fierce face, and understanding riddles, will stand up.
units.rightText: In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.

units.leftText: His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will destroy awesomely, and will prosper in what he does. He will destroy the mighty ones and the holy people.
units.rightText: His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.

units.leftText: Through his policy he will cause deceit to prosper in his hand. He will magnify himself in his heart, and he will destroy many in their security. He will also stand up against the prince of princes, but he will be broken without human hands.
units.rightText: Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.

units.leftText: “The vision of the evenings and mornings which has been told is true; but seal up the vision, for it belongs to many days to come.”
units.rightText: The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”

units.leftText: I, Daniel, fainted, and was sick for some days. Then I rose up and did the king’s business. I wondered at the vision, but no one understood it.
units.rightText: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.

units.leftText: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of the Medes, who was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans—
units.rightText: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —
rightNotes: 9:1 Hebrew Ahasuerus
9:1 That is, the Babylonians
