units.leftText: in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, understood by the books the number of the years about which the LORD’s word came to Jeremiah the prophet for the accomplishing of the desolations of Jerusalem, even seventy years.
units.rightText: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
leftNotes: 9:2 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 9:2 See Jeremiah 25:11–12|JER 25:11-12* and Jeremiah 29:10.

units.leftText: I set my face to the Lord God, to seek by prayer and petitions, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.
units.rightText: So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

units.leftText: I prayed to the LORD my God, and made confession, and said,
units.rightText: And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments,
rightNotes: 9:4 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: we have sinned, and have dealt perversely, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even turning aside from your precepts and from your ordinances.
units.rightText: we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.

units.leftText: We haven’t listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
units.rightText: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, fathers, and all the people of the land.

units.leftText: “Lord, righteousness belongs to you, but to us confusion of face, as it is today; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, who are near and who are far off, through all the countries where you have driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against you.
units.rightText: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame— the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.

units.leftText: Lord, to us belongs confusion of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against you.
units.rightText: O LORD, we are covered with shame — our kings, our leaders, and our fathers — because we have sinned against You.

units.leftText: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.
units.rightText: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him

units.leftText: We haven’t obeyed the LORD our God’s voice, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.
units.rightText: and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.

units.leftText: Yes, all Israel have transgressed your law, turning aside, and not obeying your voice.
units.rightText: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.

units.leftText: He has confirmed his words, which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing on us a great evil; for under the whole sky, such has not been done as has been done to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come on us. Yet we have not entreated the favor of the LORD our God, that we should turn from our iniquities and have discernment in your truth.
units.rightText: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD has watched over the evil, and brought it on us; for the LORD our God is righteous in all his works which he does, and we have not obeyed his voice.
units.rightText: Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.

units.leftText: “Now, Lord our God, who has brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and have gotten yourself renown, as it is today, we have sinned. We have done wickedly.
units.rightText: Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.

units.leftText: Lord, according to all your righteousness, please let your anger and your wrath be turned away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain; because for our sins and for the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to all who are around us.
units.rightText: O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.

units.leftText: “Now therefore, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his petitions, and cause your face to shine on your sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord’s sake.
units.rightText: So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.

units.leftText: My God, turn your ear and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations, and the city which is called by your name; for we do not present our petitions before you for our righteousness, but for your great mercies’ sake.
units.rightText: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.

units.leftText: Lord, hear. Lord, forgive. Lord, listen and do. Don’t defer, for your own sake, my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.”
units.rightText: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.”

units.leftText: While I was speaking, praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God—
units.rightText: While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain—

units.leftText: yes, while I was speaking in prayer—the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
units.rightText: while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.

units.leftText: He instructed me and talked with me, and said, “Daniel, I have now come to give you wisdom and understanding.
units.rightText: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.

units.leftText: At the beginning of your petitions the commandment went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are greatly beloved. Therefore consider the matter and understand the vision.
units.rightText: At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision:

units.leftText: “Seventy weeks are decreed on your people and on your holy city, to finish disobedience, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.
units.rightText: Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
rightNotes: 9:24 Or Seventy sevens; also twice in verse 25 and once in verse 26
9:24 Or the Holy of Holies or the Most Holy One; literally the Most Holy

units.leftText: “Know therefore and discern that from the going out of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem to the Anointed One, the prince, will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be built again, with street and moat, even in troubled times.
units.rightText: Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
leftNotes: 9:25 “Anointed One” can also be translated “Messiah” (same as “Christ”).
rightNotes: 9:25 Or the Anointed One; also in verse 26

units.leftText: After the sixty-two weeks the Anointed One will be cut off, and will have nothing. The people of the prince who come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will be with a flood, and war will be even to the end. Desolations are determined.
units.rightText: Then after the sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off and will have nothing.
leftNotes: 9:26 “Anointed One” can also be translated “Messiah” (same as “Christ”).
rightNotes: 9:26 Hebrew Then after sixty-two sevens

units.leftText: He will make a firm covenant with many for one week. In the middle of the week he will cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease. On the wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate; and even to the decreed full end, wrath will be poured out on the desolate.”
units.rightText: And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week, but in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him. ”
rightNotes: 9:27 Or for one seven; similarly again in this verse
9:27 Literally And on the wing (will come) the abomination that causes desolation, or And on the wing of abominations (will come) one who causes desolation,
9:27 Literally until the decreed consummation is poured out upon (him who) is desolate.

units.leftText: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the message was true, even a great warfare. He understood the message, and had understanding of the vision.
units.rightText: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true, and it concerned a great conflict. And the understanding of the message was given to him in a vision.
rightNotes: 10:1 Or true and greatly burdensome

units.leftText: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks.
units.rightText: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.

units.leftText: I ate no pleasant food. No meat or wine came into my mouth. I didn’t anoint myself at all, until three whole weeks were fulfilled.
units.rightText: I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were completed.

units.leftText: In the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel,
units.rightText: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,

units.leftText: I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a man clothed in linen, whose waist was adorned with pure gold of Uphaz.
units.rightText: I lifted up my eyes, and behold, there was a certain man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.

units.leftText: His body also was like beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches. His arms and his feet were like burnished bronze. The voice of his words was like the voice of a multitude.
units.rightText: His body was like beryl, his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.

units.leftText: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, for the men who were with me didn’t see the vision, but a great quaking fell on them, and they fled to hide themselves.
units.rightText: Only I, Daniel, saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but a great terror fell upon them, and they ran and hid themselves.

units.leftText: So I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; for my face grew deathly pale, and I retained no strength.
units.rightText: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless.

units.leftText: Yet I heard the voice of his words. When I heard the voice of his words, then I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.
units.rightText: I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.

units.leftText: Behold, a hand touched me, which set me on my knees and on the palms of my hands.
units.rightText: Suddenly, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Daniel, you greatly beloved man, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright, for I have been sent to you, now.” When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling.
units.rightText: He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man who is highly precious. Consider carefully the words that I am about to say to you. Stand up, for I have now been sent to you.”

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Don’t be afraid, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come for your words’ sake.
units.rightText: “Do not be afraid, Daniel,” he said, “for from the first day that you purposed to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.

units.leftText: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; but, behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me because I remained there with the kings of Persia.
units.rightText: However, the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.

units.leftText: Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision is yet for many days.”
units.rightText: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days.”

units.leftText: When he had spoken these words to me, I set my face toward the ground and was mute.
units.rightText: While he was speaking these words to me, I set my face toward the ground and became speechless.

units.leftText: Behold, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth, and spoke and said to him who stood before me, “My lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows have overtaken me, and I retain no strength.
units.rightText: And suddenly one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision, I am overcome with anguish, and I have no strength.
rightNotes: 10:16 Most MT manuscripts; literally with the likeness of sons of man; DSS, LXX, and one MT manuscript with the likeness of the hand of a man

units.leftText: For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? For as for me, immediately there remained no strength in me. There was no breath left in me.”
units.rightText: How can I, your servant, speak with you, my lord? Now I have no strength, nor is any breath left in me.”

units.leftText: Then one like the appearance of a man touched me again, and he strengthened me.
units.rightText: Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me.

units.leftText: He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.”
units.rightText: “Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious,” he said. “Peace be with you! Be strong now; be very strong!”

units.leftText: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, behold, the prince of Greece will come.
units.rightText: “Do you know why I have come to you?” he said. “I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I have gone forth, behold, the prince of Greece will come.
rightNotes: 10:20 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: But I will tell you that which is inscribed in the writing of truth. There is no one who holds with me against these but Michael your prince.
units.rightText: But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth. Yet no one has the courage to support me against these, except Michael your prince.[’’]

units.leftText: “As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.
units.rightText: “And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, stood up to strengthen and protect him.

units.leftText: “Now I will show you the truth. Behold, three more kings will stand up in Persia. The fourth will be far richer than all of them. When he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up all against the realm of Greece.
units.rightText: Now then, I will tell you the truth: Three more kings will arise in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. By the power of his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
rightNotes: 11:2 Hebrew of Javan

units.leftText: A mighty king will stand up, who will rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.
units.rightText: Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great authority and do as he pleases.

units.leftText: When he stands up, his kingdom will be broken and will be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, even for others besides these.
units.rightText: But as soon as he is established, his kingdom will be broken up and parceled out toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the authority with which he ruled, because his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others.

units.leftText: “The king of the south will be strong. One of his princes will become stronger than him, and have dominion. His dominion will be a great dominion.
units.rightText: The king of the South will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow even stronger and will rule his own kingdom with great authority.

units.leftText: At the end of years they will join themselves together; and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain the strength of her arm. He will also not stand, nor will his arm; but she will be given up, with those who brought her, and he who became the father of her, and he who strengthened her in those times.
units.rightText: After some years they will form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South will go to the king of the North to seal the agreement. But his daughter will not retain her position of power, nor will his strength endure. At that time she will be given up, along with her royal escort and her father and the one who supported her.
rightNotes: 11:6 Or offspring
11:6 Or child; see Vulgate and Syriac.

units.leftText: “But out of a shoot from her roots one will stand up in his place, who will come to the army and will enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and will deal against them and will prevail.
units.rightText: But one from her family line will rise up in his place, come against the army of the king of the North, and enter his fortress, fighting and prevailing.
rightNotes: 11:7 Literally a branch from her roots

units.leftText: He will also carry their gods with their molten images, and with their goodly vessels of silver and of gold, captive into Egypt. He will refrain some years from the king of the north.
units.rightText: He will take even their gods captive to Egypt, with their metal images and their precious vessels of silver and gold. For some years he will stay away from the king of the North,

units.leftText: He will come into the realm of the king of the south, but he will return into his own land.
units.rightText: who will invade the realm of the king of the South and then return to his own land.

units.leftText: His sons will wage war, and will assemble a multitude of great forces which will come on, and overflow, and pass through. They will return and wage war, even to his fortress.
units.rightText: But his sons will stir up strife and assemble a great army, which will advance forcefully, sweeping through like a flood, and will again carry the battle as far as his fortress.

units.leftText: “The king of the south will be moved with anger and will come out and fight with him, even with the king of the north. He will send out a great multitude, and the multitude will be given into his hand.
units.rightText: In a rage, the king of the South will march out to fight the king of the North, who will raise a large army, but it will be delivered into the hand of his enemy.

units.leftText: The multitude will be carried off, and his heart will be exalted. He will cast down tens of thousands, but he won’t prevail.
units.rightText: When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be proud in heart and will cast down tens of thousands, but he will not triumph.

units.leftText: The king of the north will return, and will send out a multitude greater than the former. He will come on at the end of the times, even of years, with a great army and with abundant supplies.
units.rightText: For the king of the North will raise another army, larger than the first, and after some years he will advance with a great army and many supplies.
rightNotes: 11:13 Hebrew at the end of the times

units.leftText: “In those times many will stand up against the king of the south. Also the children of the violent among your people will lift themselves up to establish the vision, but they will fall.
units.rightText: In those times many will rise up against the king of the South. Violent ones among your own people will exalt themselves in fulfillment of the vision, but they will fail.

units.leftText: So the king of the north will come and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified city. The forces of the south won’t stand, neither will his select troops, neither will there be any strength to stand.
units.rightText: Then the king of the North will come, build up a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will not stand; even their best troops will not be able to resist.

units.leftText: But he who comes against him will do according to his own will, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the glorious land, and destruction will be in his hand.
units.rightText: The invader will do as he pleases, and no one will stand against him. He will establish himself in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.

units.leftText: He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions. He will perform them. He will give him the daughter of women, to destroy the kingdom, but she will not stand, and won’t be for him.
units.rightText: He will resolve to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and will reach an agreement with the king of the South. He will give him a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, but his plan will not succeed or help him.
rightNotes: 11:17 Or but she will not stand with him or support him

units.leftText: After this he will turn his face to the islands, and will take many, but a prince will cause the reproach offered by him to cease. Yes, moreover, he will cause his reproach to turn on him.
units.rightText: Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many of them. But a commander will put an end to his reproach and will turn it back upon him.

units.leftText: Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he will stumble and fall, and won’t be found.
units.rightText: After this, he will turn back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be no more.

units.leftText: “Then one who will cause a tax collector to pass through the kingdom to maintain its glory will stand up in his place; but within a few days he shall be destroyed, not in anger, and not in battle.
units.rightText: In his place one will arise who will send out a tax collector for the glory of the kingdom; but within a few days he will be destroyed, though not in anger or in battle.

units.leftText: “In his place a contemptible person will stand up, to whom they had not given the honor of the kingdom; but he will come in a time of security, and will obtain the kingdom by flatteries.
units.rightText: In his place a despicable person will arise; royal honors will not be given to him, but he will come in a time of peace and seize the kingdom by intrigue.

units.leftText: The overwhelming forces will be overwhelmed from before him, and will be broken. Yes, also the prince of the covenant.
units.rightText: Then a flood of forces will be swept away before him and destroyed, along with a prince of the covenant.

units.leftText: After the treaty made with him he will work deceitfully; for he will come up and will become strong with few people.
units.rightText: After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully; for he will rise to power with only a few people.

units.leftText: In a time of security he will come even on the fattest places of the province. He will do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers. He will scatter among them prey, plunder, and wealth. Yes, he will devise his plans against the strongholds, but only for a time.
units.rightText: In a time of peace, he will invade the richest provinces and do what his fathers and forefathers never did. He will lavish plunder, loot, and wealth on his followers, and he will plot against the strongholds — but only for a time.

units.leftText: “He will stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south will wage war in battle with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he won’t stand; for they will devise plans against him.
units.rightText: And with a large army he will stir up his power and his courage against the king of the South, who will mobilize a very large and powerful army but will not withstand the plots devised against him.

units.leftText: Yes, those who eat of his delicacies will destroy him, and his army will be swept away. Many will fall down slain.
units.rightText: Those who eat from his provisions will seek to destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.

units.leftText: As for both these kings, their hearts will be to do evil, and they will speak lies at one table; but it won’t prosper, for the end will still be at the appointed time.
units.rightText: And the two kings, with their hearts bent on evil, will speak lies at the same table, but to no avail, for still the end will come at the appointed time.

units.leftText: Then he will return into his land with great wealth. His heart will be against the holy covenant. He will take action, and return to his own land.
units.rightText: The king of the North will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant; so he will do damage and return to his own land.

units.leftText: “He will return at the appointed time and come into the south; but it won’t be in the latter time as it was in the former.
units.rightText: At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but this time will not be like the first.

units.leftText: For ships of Kittim will come against him. Therefore he will be grieved, and will return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and will take action. He will even return, and have regard to those who forsake the holy covenant.
units.rightText: Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and rage against the holy covenant and do damage. So he will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
rightNotes: 11:30 Or western coastlands or Mediterranean islands

units.leftText: “Forces from him will profane the sanctuary, even the fortress, and will take away the continual burnt offering. Then they will set up the abomination that makes desolate.
units.rightText: His forces will rise up and desecrate the temple fortress. They will abolish the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.

units.leftText: He will corrupt those who do wickedly against the covenant by flatteries; but the people who know their God will be strong and take action.
units.rightText: With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will firmly resist him.

units.leftText: “Those who are wise among the people will instruct many; yet they will fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, many days.
units.rightText: Those with insight will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by sword or flame, or be captured or plundered.

units.leftText: Now when they fall, they will be helped with a little help; but many will join themselves to them with flatteries.
units.rightText: Now when they fall, they will be granted a little help, but many will join them insincerely.

units.leftText: Some of those who are wise will fall—to refine them, and to purify, and to make them white, even to the time of the end, because it is yet for the time appointed.
units.rightText: Some of the wise will fall so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless until the time of the end, for it will still come at the appointed time.

units.leftText: “The king will do according to his will. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and will speak marvelous things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the indignation is accomplished, for that which is determined will be done.
units.rightText: Then the king will do as he pleases and will exalt and magnify himself above every god, and he will speak monstrous things against the God of gods. He will be successful until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been decreed must be accomplished.

units.leftText: He won’t regard the gods of his fathers, or the desire of women, or regard any god; for he will magnify himself above all.
units.rightText: He will show no regard for the gods of his fathers, nor for the one desired by women, nor for any other god, because he will magnify himself above them all.

units.leftText: But in their place, he will honor the god of fortresses. He will honor a god whom his fathers didn’t know with gold, silver, and with precious stones and pleasant things.
units.rightText: And in their place, he will honor a god of fortresses— a god his fathers did not know— with gold, silver, precious stones, and riches.

units.leftText: He will deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god. He will increase with glory whoever acknowledges him. He will cause them to rule over many, and will divide the land for a price.
units.rightText: He will attack the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god and will greatly honor those who acknowledge him, making them rulers over many and distributing the land for a price.
rightNotes: 11:39 Or for a reward

units.leftText: “At the time of the end the king of the south will contend with him; and the king of the north will come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, with horsemen, and with many ships. He will enter into the countries, and will overflow and pass through.
units.rightText: At the time of the end, the king of the South will engage him in battle, but the king of the North will storm out against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships, invading many countries and sweeping through them like a flood.
rightNotes: 11:40 Hebrew will thrust at him

units.leftText: He will enter also into the glorious land, and many countries will be overthrown; but these will be delivered out of his hand: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
units.rightText: He will also invade the Beautiful Land, and many countries will fall. But these will be delivered from his hand: Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites.

units.leftText: He will also stretch out his hand on the countries. The land of Egypt won’t escape.
units.rightText: He will extend his power over many countries, and not even the land of Egypt will escape.

units.leftText: But he will have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt. The Libyans and the Ethiopians will follow his steps.
units.rightText: He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and over all the riches of Egypt, and the Libyans and Cushites will also submit to him.
rightNotes: 11:43 That is, people from the upper Nile region

units.leftText: But news out of the east and out of the north will trouble him; and he will go out with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many.
units.rightText: But news from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out with great fury to destroy many and devote them to destruction.
rightNotes: 11:44 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: He will plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.
units.rightText: He will pitch his royal tents between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain, but he will meet his end with no one to help him.[’’]

units.leftText: “At that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there will be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time. At that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.
units.rightText: “At that time Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress, the likes of which will not have occurred from the beginning of nations until that time. But at that time your people — everyone whose name is found written in the book — will be delivered.

units.leftText: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
units.rightText: And many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt.
rightNotes: 12:2 See John 5:29|JHN 5:29* and Revelation 11:18.

units.leftText: Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.
units.rightText: Then the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
rightNotes: 12:3 Or expanse or firmament; see also Genesis 1:6–8|GEN 1:6-8*.
12:3 See Matthew 13:43|MAT 13:43*.

units.leftText: But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book, even to the time of the end. Many will run back and forth, and knowledge will be increased.”
units.rightText: But you, Daniel, shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will roam to and fro, and knowledge will increase.”

units.leftText: Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others stood, one on the river bank on this side, and the other on the river bank on that side.
units.rightText: Then I, Daniel, looked and saw two others standing there, one on this bank of the river and one on the opposite bank.

units.leftText: One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long will it be to the end of these wonders?”
units.rightText: One of them said to the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long until the fulfillment of these wonders?”

units.leftText: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it will be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have finished breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things will be finished.
units.rightText: And the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by Him who lives forever, saying, “It will be for a time, and times, and half a time. When the power of the holy people has finally been shattered, all these things will be completed.”

units.leftText: I heard, but I didn’t understand. Then I said, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”
units.rightText: I heard, but I did not understand. So I asked, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”

units.leftText: He said, “Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
units.rightText: “Go on your way, Daniel,” he replied, “for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.

units.leftText: Many will purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined, but the wicked will do wickedly; and none of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
units.rightText: Many will be purified, made spotless, and refined, but the wicked will continue to act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand.

units.leftText: “From the time that the continual burnt offering is taken away and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
units.rightText: And from the time the daily sacrifice is abolished and the abomination of desolation set up, there will be 1,290 days.

units.leftText: Blessed is he who waits, and comes to the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
units.rightText: Blessed is he who waits and reaches the end of the 1,335 days.

units.leftText: “But go your way until the end; for you will rest, and will stand in your inheritance at the end of the days.”
units.rightText: But as for you, go on your way until the end. You will rest, and then you will arise to your inheritance at the end of the days.”
